title: Jesus and Israel: One Covenant or Two?
author: David E. Holwerda
summary: Argues that Jesus fulfils Israel's identity, land, temple and law, so that God's promises to Israel are kept in Christ, while also discussing the place of the Jewish people in Romans 11.

title: The Promise of the Future
author: Cornelis P. Venema
summary: A Reformed amillennial survey of eschatology, including chapters on the future of Israel, the millennium and the new creation.

title: The Gospel and the Land: Early Christianity and Jewish Territorial Doctrine
author: W. D. Davies
summary: A major historical study of how the New Testament writers treated the land promise, concluding that they largely transferred holy-space concerns to the person of Christ.

title: Whose Land? Whose Promise? What Christians Are Not Being Told about Israel and the Palestinians
author: Gary M. Burge
summary: Examines the biblical land promises and their application in the New Testament, and criticises Christian Zionist readings of the modern conflict, with attention to Palestinian Christians.

title: Bound for the Promised Land: The Land Promise in God's Redemptive Plan
author: Oren R. Martin
summary: A volume in the New Studies in Biblical Theology series tracing the land promise from Eden through Canaan to the new creation in Christ.

title: Romans (Baker Exegetical Commentary on the New Testament)
author: Thomas R. Schreiner
summary: A detailed exegetical commentary on Romans which argues that Romans 11:26 foresees a future large-scale salvation of ethnic Jews through faith in Christ.

title: Future Israel: Why Christian Anti-Judaism Must Be Challenged
author: Barry E. Horner
summary: A premillennial, Calvinistic defence of a continuing future for ethnic and national Israel, critical of supersessionist readings in church history.

title: Israelology: The Missing Link in Systematic Theology
author: Arnold G. Fruchtenbaum
summary: A Messianic Jewish dispensational systematic study of Israel past, present and future, arguing for a permanent distinction between Israel and the church.

title: The Promise-Plan of God: A Biblical Theology of the Old and New Testaments
author: Walter C. Kaiser Jr.
summary: Traces one unified promise-plan through Scripture and argues that the promises to Israel, including the land, remain part of that plan.

title: The New Christian Zionism: Fresh Perspectives on Israel and the Land
author: Gerald R. McDermott (ed.)
summary: Essays by several scholars arguing for a continuing theological significance of the Jewish people and the land without depending on a full dispensational system.

title: In Defense of Israel
author: John Hagee
summary: A popular case by the founder of Christians United for Israel for Christian support of the Jewish people and the State of Israel on biblical grounds.

title: Christian Zionism: Road-map to Armageddon?
author: Stephen Sizer
summary: A critical history and theological assessment of Christian Zionism from its nineteenth-century roots to its modern political influence.

title: The Davidic Promise and the Inclusion of the Gentiles (Amos 9:9-15 and Acts 15:13-18): A Test Passage for Theological Systems
author: Walter C. Kaiser Jr.
summary: Journal of the Evangelical Theological Society 20/2. Kaiser argues James sees the Gentile mission as part of the rebuilding of David's house, while the promise to Israel still stands.

title: James and the Gentiles (Acts 15.13-21)
author: Richard Bauckham
summary: Essay in History, Literature and Society in the Book of Acts, ed. Ben Witherington III. Bauckham argues James reads the rebuilt tent of David as the eschatological temple, the community of Jews and Gentiles.

title: Israel in Prophecy
author: John F. Walvoord
summary: A dispensational exposition of the Abrahamic, Davidic and new covenants, arguing for Israel's future national regathering and kingdom.

title: An Old Testament Theology: An Exegetical, Canonical, and Thematic Approach
author: Bruce K. Waltke (with Charles Yu)
summary: A major Old Testament theology. Its chapters on the land argue that the New Testament redefines the land promise in Christ, as heavenly and finally the renewed earth.

title: Sealed with an Oath: Covenant in God's Unfolding Purpose
author: Paul R. Williamson
summary: New Studies in Biblical Theology 23. A survey of the biblical covenants, including the Abrahamic oath and its national and international strands.

title: On the Reliability of the Old Testament
author: K. A. Kitchen
summary: An Egyptologist's survey of archaeological and textual evidence for the Old Testament periods, from the patriarchs to the exile and return.

title: The Tel Dan Stele (Aramaic inscription naming 'the house of David')
author: Aramean king, probably Hazael of Damascus; published by Avraham Biran and Joseph Naveh
summary: Fragments found at Tel Dan in 1993 and 1994, now in the Israel Museum. The earliest known extra-biblical reference to David's dynasty (bytdwd).

title: The Cyrus Cylinder
author: Cyrus II of Persia (inscription)
summary: A clay cylinder found at Babylon in 1879, now in the British Museum. It records Cyrus's conquest of Babylon and his policy of returning displaced peoples and their gods to their homes.

title: Assyrian and Babylonian Chronicles
author: A. K. Grayson
summary: A standard edition of the Mesopotamian chronicles, including the Babylonian Chronicle (ABC 5) that dates Nebuchadnezzar's capture of Jerusalem to 2 Adar 597 BC.

title: The Coming Prince
author: Sir Robert Anderson
summary: Classic calculation of Daniel's seventy weeks using 360-day prophetic years from Artaxerxes' decree to Nehemiah, ending at the triumphal entry, with the seventieth week placed in the future.

title: Jesus and the Land: The New Testament Challenge to 'Holy Land' Theology
author: Gary M. Burge
summary: Argues that the New Testament relocates the holiness of the land to Jesus himself and widens the inheritance to the world, challenging theologies that make the modern territory theologically central.

title: Der Judenstaat (The Jewish State)
author: Theodor Herzl
summary: Herzl's founding pamphlet of political Zionism, arguing that antisemitism made a Jewish state, secured by international agreement, a practical necessity.

title: The Balfour Declaration (letter to Lord Rothschild, 2 November 1917)
author: Arthur James Balfour
summary: British government statement favouring a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine, with a proviso protecting the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities.

title: United Nations General Assembly Resolution 181 (II): Future Government of Palestine
author: United Nations General Assembly
summary: The partition plan recommending separate Jewish and Arab states and an international regime for Jerusalem, adopted 29 November 1947 by 33 votes to 13 with 10 abstentions.

title: Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel
author: Provisional State Council of Israel
summary: The founding declaration read by David Ben-Gurion on 14 May 1948, grounding the state in Jewish history, the Balfour Declaration, the Holocaust and the UN resolution.

title: The Origins of Christian Zionism: Lord Shaftesbury and Evangelical Support for a Jewish Homeland
author: Donald M. Lewis
summary: A historian's study of British evangelical restorationism, centred on Shaftesbury, and its role in the background to Zionism.

title: 1948: A History of the First Arab-Israeli War
author: Benny Morris
summary: A detailed military and political history of the 1947-49 war, including the causes of the Palestinian refugee exodus.

title: Israel: A History
author: Anita Shapira
summary: A general history of Zionism and the State of Israel from the 1880s to the early twenty-first century.

title: A History of Zionism
author: Walter Laqueur
summary: A standard history of the Zionist movement from its nineteenth-century roots to the founding of the state.

title: Messianism, Zionism, and Jewish Religious Radicalism
author: Aviezer Ravitzky
summary: Analyses the range of Orthodox Jewish responses to Zionism, from Haredi opposition (including Satmar) to Rabbi Kook's religious Zionism.

title: Vayoel Moshe
author: Joel Teitelbaum (the Satmar Rebbe)
summary: A Hebrew treatise arguing from Jewish law and tradition that establishing a Jewish state before the coming of the Messiah is forbidden.

title: "A Land without a People for a People without a Land"
author: Diana Muir
summary: Middle East Quarterly article tracing the origin and use of the slogan, including its links with Alexander Keith, Shaftesbury and Israel Zangwill.

title: Apocalypsis Apocalypseos (A Revelation of the Revelation)
author: Thomas Brightman
summary: An influential Puritan commentary on Revelation that expected the conversion of the Jews and their return to the land.

title: The Mystery of Israel's Salvation Explained and Applyed
author: Increase Mather
summary: A New England Puritan's case for a future national conversion of the Jews and their restoration.

title: Jesus Is Coming
author: William E. Blackstone
summary: A widely circulated premillennial book by the author of the 1891 Blackstone Memorial, teaching Israel's restoration as a sign of the end.

title: Jerusalem Countdown: A Warning to the World
author: John Hagee
summary: A popular Christian Zionist book by the founder of Christians United for Israel, reading current Middle East events through prophecy.

title: The Davidic Promise and the Inclusion of the Gentiles (Amos 9:9-15 and Acts 15:13-18): A Test Passage for Theological Systems
author: Walter C. Kaiser Jr.
summary: A Journal of the Evangelical Theological Society article arguing that Acts 15 confirms the Gentile part of Amos 9 while the national promise remains.

title: Epicenter: Why the Current Rumblings in the Middle East Will Change Your Future
author: Joel C. Rosenberg
summary: A popular book reading Ezekiel 38-39 as a coming invasion of Israel by Russia, Iran and allies.

title: Eye to Eye: Facing the Consequences of Dividing Israel
author: William R. Koenig
summary: Argues from Joel 3:2 and Genesis 12:3 that pressure on Israel to divide the land has been followed by disasters.

title: The Last Word on the Middle East
author: Derek Prince
summary: A Pentecostal Bible teacher's case that Israel's regathering fulfils prophecy and that Christians should support it.

title: The Politics of Christian Zionism, 1891-1948
author: Paul C. Merkley
summary: A historian's account of Christian Zionist influence on British and American policy from the Blackstone Memorial to 1948.

title: Evangelicals and Israel: The Story of American Christian Zionism
author: Stephen Spector
summary: A study of American Christian Zionism's beliefs, motives and political influence, based on extensive interviews.

title: Christ and Time: The Primitive Christian Conception of Time and History
author: Oscar Cullmann
summary: Swiss New Testament scholar who argued that the decisive battle of salvation history was won at the cross and resurrection, while the final victory waits for Christ's return; his D-Day and V-Day picture shaped the later 'already / not yet' consensus.

title: The Teaching of Jesus Concerning the Kingdom of God and the Church
author: Geerhardus Vos
summary: Short study by the Princeton biblical theologian arguing that Jesus taught the kingdom as both present in his ministry and future in its consummation, and that the church is the present form of the kingdom.

title: The Greatness of the Kingdom: An Inductive Study of the Kingdom of God
author: Alva J. McClain
summary: Classic dispensational study tracing the mediatorial kingdom from the Old Testament through its offer and postponement in the Gospels to its establishment in the millennium.

title: Continuity and Discontinuity: Perspectives on the Relationship Between the Old and New Testaments
author: John S. Feinberg (editor)
summary: Essays in honour of S. Lewis Johnson in which covenant and dispensational scholars debate in pairs; it includes Bruce Waltke's essay 'Kingdom Promises as Spiritual' and dispensational essays on the same questions.

title: The God of Israel and Christian Theology
author: R. Kendall Soulen
summary: A study of supersessionism in Christian theology, distinguishing several kinds and proposing a reading of the canon that keeps God's covenant with Israel central.

title: Toward an Old Testament Theology
author: Walter C. Kaiser Jr.
summary: Presents the Old Testament as one unfolding promise-plan of God, with the promise of land and nation to Israel as a lasting part of that plan.
